newsitem.title: USA: Schuller changes name back to Johns-Manville.
newsitem.headline: Schuller changes name back to Johns-Manville.

text.p: Schuller Corp., the insulation and building products maker, said Monday it will change its name back to Johns-Manville Corp., its corporate predecessor that was once a leading supplier of asbestos insulation.

The building products company, which was founded in 1858 as H.W. Johns Manufacturing Co., has seen several name changes. The firm changed its name to Johns-Manville Corp. in 1901, and then to Manville Corp. in 1981.

Manville filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in 1982 to shield itself from about 17,000 lawsuits filed over asbestos-related claims, even though at the time it had $2.2 billion in sales and $60 million in profits the previous year.
It emerged from bankruptcy in 1988, after creating a separate trust fund to settle the remaining asbestos claims.

In 1991 Manville became a holding company with two operating subsidiaries, Riverwood International, which made paperboard and packaging, and Schuller. It sold a controlling interest in Riverwood last March to Clayton Dubilier & Rice for $1.1 billion and subsequently adopted the Schuller name for the holding company.

"We have conducted considerable research which shows that customers, suppliers, do-it-yourselfers and the general public all have a high level of favourable awareness toward the Johns-Manville identity," said company Chairman Charles Henry.
"These results clearly suggest that renaming the company Johns-Manville will help strengthen market share and drive growth in our business ... Most people know or think of us as Johns-Manville.
"That identity has a much higher favourable awareness than the Schuller name," Henry said.
In the markets served by Schuller GmbH, its German subsidiary, the company will retain the Schuller name.
The change is subject to shareholder approval at its May 2 annual meeting.
Schuller's stock lost 50 cents to end at $11.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
